summary: Mostly no. On BTC, ETH and SOL, price crossing up through resistance and price crossing down through resistance did the same as random entries on 1h, 4h and daily. The result that holds up is price crossing back up through support on 1h: 20 candles later it was 0.38% ahead of random entries, and the gap held without its strongest stretch.

verdicts.use: Buying a cross back up through support
verdicts.text: Beat random on 1h by 0.38% after 20 candles. It held without its strongest stretch and again at 50 candles. On 4h and daily it did the same as random.
Same as random on 1h, 4h and daily with the default pivots. The 5-bar version beat random on daily only because of signals between Aug 6 and Aug 27, 2021.
Worse than random on 1h by 0.19%, but only at 20 candles, so the result is fragile. On 4h and daily it did the same as random.

verdicts.use: Shorting a cross down through resistance
verdicts.text: Same as random on 1h, 4h and daily.

notes: Price crossing up through support on 1h gave 1,768 entries in 983 separate moves. Twenty candles later, those entries were 0.38% ahead of random entries, above a luck band that tops out at 0.23%. Without its strongest stretch, signals on Sep 17, 2021, the result held. It also showed at 50 candles but not at 10 or 100. On each coin alone the result was weaker. BTC and ETH stayed inside the luck band, and SOL's 0.58% showed at 20 candles only.

The same 1h support cross did better in downtrends than in uptrends. Below the 200-day average, entries were 0.42% ahead of random. That result held without its strongest stretch, signals on Feb 24, 2022, the day Russia invaded Ukraine, and showed at 10, 20 and 50 candles. Above the average, entries were 0.4% ahead, but only at 20 candles, so the uptrend result is fragile.

On slower candles, the support cross did the same as random. With the default pivots, the 4h version was 0.5% behind random and the daily version was 0.68% ahead, both inside the luck band. With 5-bar pivots on 4h, the pooled result was the same as random. In downtrends, though, the 5-bar version was 1.18% ahead, held without signals on May 5–6, 2025, and showed at 10, 20 and 50 candles. In uptrends, the same setting did the same as random.

Shorting as price crossed down through support on 1h gave 2,481 entries that did 0.19% worse than random. The pooled result showed only at 20 candles. In uptrends the short did 0.28% worse, held without its strongest stretch, and showed at 10 and 20 candles. In downtrends it did the same as random. In uptrends, price that broke support tended to recover rather than keep falling.

Price crossing up through resistance on 1h fired about one and a half times as often as the support cross. Its 2,639 entries landed at exactly 0% against random. On 4h it was 0.65% ahead, just inside a luck band that reaches 0.69%. The 5-bar version fires about twice as often on 1h and also did the same as random. On daily, the 5-bar version beat random by 2.97%, but only because of signals between Aug 6 and Aug 27, 2021. Shorting a cross down through resistance did the same as random on every timeframe.

On a long 1h bot, a cross back up through support is a candidate filter to test beside your other start conditions, and it showed more in downtrends. The gap is under half a percent after 20 candles, so your take profit and DCA orders still decide most of each deal. Resistance breakouts added no timing information on these pairs, so you can leave them out. On a short bot, opening on a break below support in an uptrend did worse than random entries.
